text:
liz: Bringing up cumulus-edge-8b for a quick eval run. License looks kinda nonstandard — need a legal sanity check before we start quant experiments or artifact caching. Anyone from legal available?

santiago: Which license? Can you paste the LICENSE.md or link?

liz: Repo and LICENSE: https://hf.co/cumulus/cumulus-edge-8b — key parts below:
```
# LICENSE excerpt
No commercial hosting or distribution.
Redistribution of weights allowed for research use only.
Attribution required: include model name and creator link.
```

julia (legal): Thanks — quick read now. Can you paste the exact clause that defines "research" (if any)? If not, I can give a conservative interpretation.

liz: There's no formal definition beyond "research use" and an examples paragraph that lists "academic labs, internal experiments". No explicit exceptions for private deployments.

julia (legal): Quick take: "No commercial hosting" means we cannot offer this model via our hosted API or Dedicated offerings where customers pay for access. Private/Customer-managed VPC hosting is a borderline case — if the model only runs inside a named customer's environment under their contract (and we're not reselling access), it's generally allowed.

However, the redistribution phrase is the kicker: generating and shipping quantized weight files is almost certainly a derivative redistribution. If the license restricts redistribution to "research use only", we should NOT publish quantized weights or make them downloadable to third parties. Internal caching is okay if access is strictly controlled.

mike: To clarify — serving the quantized model inside a customer's VPC (Redwood Private) — is that considered "hosting" or "reselling"? We plan to do per-customer deployment and bill infra.

julia (legal): If the customer is the only tenant and the deployment is strictly for that customer (and you don't advertise the model as part of a public hosted product), that's typically acceptable. The problem is offering it as a multi-tenant, metered hosted product. If you plan to bill for inference as a Redwood product, we need a license exception from upstream.

santiago: We wanted to cache int8 artifacts in our internal artifacts bucket to speed rollout. Is that "redistribution"?

julia (legal): Internal caching for performance is allowed provided: (1) artifacts are access-restricted, (2) we document provenance, and (3) artifacts aren't exported. Treat quantized files as "restricted" and add audit logs for access. Do not allow downloads or export in customer deliverables.

liz: Noted. Also the attribution clause — what's the recommended copy? The license asks to "credit original authors and include link" but doesn't specify format.

julia (legal): Use a concise attribution we can bake into UI/metadata. Example: "Model: cumulus-edge-8b — courtesy of Cumulus Research (https://hf.co/cumulus/cumulus-edge-8b)". I'll draft a legal-approved boilerplate and post it here.

ops-bot: deploy-checker: WARNING — ACLs missing for s3://artifacts/restricted/cumulus-edge-8b/quant-int8.

mike: I'll lock ACLs and tag the artifact path as "restricted" and add a non-export policy. Also enabling bucket-level logging.

santiago: Great. Next steps — block any plan to offer this on-hosted or dedicated channels; proceed with on-prem / customer-VPC evals only. I'll update the model onboarding doc and add a compliance checklist entry describing "no hosted offering" + required attribution + restricted artifact handling.

liz: Thanks all — will pause public-facing trials and start quant experiments under the restricted process. Will share results in a private doc. :thumbsup:
